input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

phyloplace_input.description: Path to a sample sheet (CSV, TSV, YAML or JSON) containing information about phylogenetic placements to perform.
phyloplace_input.help_text: This specifies parameters for direct phylogenetic placement of query sequences onto a reference phylogeny, in contrast to when a HMMER search is first performed, see `--phylosearch_input`. The format is taken from the file extension: `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.yml`/`.yaml` or `.json`. A CSV or TSV file needs at least five columns, and a header row ('sample', 'queryseqfile', 'refseqfile', 'refphylogeny' and 'model'); a YAML or JSON file is a list of entries with the same keys. See [usage docs](https://nf-co.re/phyloplace/usage#samplesheet-input-for-phylogenetic-placement).

phylosearch_input.description: Comma-separated list of target sheets (CSV, TSV, YAML or JSON) containing information about phylogenetic searches to perform.
phylosearch_input.help_text: This specifies parameters for phylogenetic placement of unknown sequences onto reference phylogeny after first using HMMER to search through a collection of unknown sequences (see `--search_fasta`) in contrast to when only placing known query sequences, see `--phyloplace_input`. The format of each file is taken from its extension: `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.yml`/`.yaml` or `.json`, and the formats can be mixed. A CSV or TSV file needs at least two columns that specify search HMM profiles ('target' and 'hmm') and at least three columns specifying the reference phylogenies ('refseqfile', 'refphylogeny' and 'model') for placement of search results; a YAML or JSON file is a list of entries with the same keys. (Decoy profiles, i.e. profiles only used for searches, not placements, are allowed.) Several files can be given as a comma-separated list, for example a collection of reference phylogenies together with your own profiles; target names must then be unique across all files. Relative paths in a file are resolved against the directory Nextflow is launched from, so a file that is shared between users should use absolute paths or URLs. See [usage docs](https://nf-co.re/phyloplace/usage#target-sheet-input-for-search-followed-by-phylogenetic-placement).

phylosearch_targets.description: Comma-separated list of targets to use from the `--phylosearch_input` files.
phylosearch_targets.help_text: By default, all targets in the `--phylosearch_input` files are searched for. Use this parameter to keep only the listed targets, for example a few from a large collection of reference phylogenies. Targets are named in the 'target' column. Every name must exist in the input files. Note that dropping a target also drops its profile from the ranking of hits across profiles.

search_fasta.description: Fasta file with sequences to be searched with HMM profiles.
search_fasta.help_text: Sequences from this file matching an HMM profile, will be placed in the reference phylogeny corresponding to the HMM profile.
search_fasta.errorMessage: FASTA file to search with the HMM profiles: extension .fa, .fna, .faa or .fasta, optionally gzipped (.gz); no other compression format is supported.

save_domtblout.description: Save the per-domain hit table (`--domtblout`) from hmmsearch.
save_domtblout.help_text: In "search and place" mode, also write hmmsearch's per-domain hit table, one gzipped `*.domtbl.gz` file per profile, to the `hmmer` output directory. Unlike the per-sequence table, this one carries alignment coordinates for each domain, which are needed to work out profile coverage or to find genes split over several ORFs.

alignmethod.description: Method used to align query sequences with.
alignmethod.help_text: Query sequences will be aligned to the reference alignment using either HMMER, Clustal Omega or MAFFT, except when an hmm profile is provided (--hmmfile; implies that --alignmethod is set to 'hmmer'), in which case both the reference and query sequences will be aligned with the profile (reference sequences must not be aligned, i.e. must not contain '-' characters). The hmm column of a --phylosearch_input target sheet is used for the search only and does not imply 'hmmer': a row without a value in its alignmethod column is aligned with the default, 'clustalo'.

min_query_columns.description: Minimum number of residues a query sequence must have in the reference columns.
min_query_columns.help_text: Before placement, query sequences are checked against the columns of the alignment that the reference sequences occupy (columns with only gaps in the reference are ignored by EPA-NG). A query with fewer residues in those columns than this value is dropped with a warning, and listed in the `filterquery` output. The default of 1 only removes queries with no residue at all in those columns, which EPA-NG cannot place and which otherwise stop the whole run. Can be set per row in the `min_query_columns` column of a `--phyloplace_input` or `--phylosearch_input` sheet.

min_reference_coverage.description: Minimum fraction of the reference columns in which a query sequence must have a residue.
min_reference_coverage.help_text: The reference coverage of a query is the number of residues it has in the columns that the reference sequences occupy, divided by the number of such columns. A query below this value is dropped with a warning, and listed in the `filterquery` output. The default of 0 turns the coverage filter off. Can be set per row in the `min_reference_coverage` column of a `--phyloplace_input` or `--phylosearch_input` sheet.

queryseqfile.errorMessage: FASTA file with query sequences: extension .fa, .fna, .faa or .fasta, optionally gzipped (.gz); no other compression format is supported.

refseqfile.description: File with reference sequences. Any format supported by HMMER tools.
refseqfile.help_text: The sequences must be aligned, except with --hmmfile (or the hmmfile column of a --phyloplace_input sample sheet), where they must be unaligned. In a --phylosearch_input target sheet they are always aligned. When refseqfile is FASTA and --taxonomy is not given, taxonomy is instead derived from each record's own header, GTDB-style ('>id taxonomy;string').
refseqfile.errorMessage: Multiple sequence alignment of the reference sequences: extension .aln, .alnfa, .alnfaa, .alnfna, .mfa, .fa, .fna, .faa, .fasta, .ph, .phy or .phylip, optionally gzipped (.gz); no other compression format is supported.

hmmfile.description: HMM file. If provided, will be used to align both the reference and query sequences.
hmmfile.errorMessage: HMM profile file: extension .hmm, optionally gzipped (.gz); no other compression format is supported.

refphylogeny.description: Newick file with the reference phylogeny.
refphylogeny.errorMessage: Newick file with the reference phylogeny: extension .newick, .nwk or .tree, optionally gzipped (.gz); no other compression format is supported.

model.description: Evolutionary model to use for placement, e.g. 'LG'.

taxonomy.description: Tab-separated file with taxonomy assignments of reference sequences.
taxonomy.help_text: The first column should consist of names of reference sequences, the second of taxonomy strings, e.g. 'Bacteria;Proteobacteria;Gammaproteobacteria;Enterobacterales;Enterobacteriaceae;Escherichia;Escherichia coli'. If omitted and refseqfile is FASTA, taxonomy is instead derived from each record's own header. If both are given, this file wins (a warning is logged if the headers also carry embedded taxonomy text).
taxonomy.errorMessage: Optional tab-separated taxonomy file: extension .tsv or .tax, optionally gzipped (.gz); no other compression format is supported.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

epa_ng_options.title: EPA-ng options
epa_ng_options.description: Settings for the phylogenetic placement with EPA-ng.

epang_filter_max.description: Maximum number of placements EPA-ng keeps per query sequence. EPA-ng's own default is 7.
epang_filter_max.help_text: A query sequence whose likelihood weight is spread over many branches keeps at most this many placements, so the accumulated likelihood weight (aLWR) in the Gappa taxonomy output can be low even when all the placements are in the same clade. Raise this together with `--epang_filter_acc_lwr` to keep more of the weight. Not set by default, which leaves EPA-ng's own default.

epang_filter_acc_lwr.description: Accumulated likelihood weight after which EPA-ng discards further placements of a query sequence.
epang_filter_acc_lwr.help_text: For example 0.99 keeps placements until they hold 99% of the likelihood weight, but never more than `--epang_filter_max`, which is 7 unless set. Not set by default, which leaves EPA-ng's own default of discarding placements with a likelihood weight below 0.01.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

modules_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of shared module test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
